provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Graduation art plan
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state their graduation art idea
The pupils should be able to list materials needed for their art

Introduction:
We love to make art. Today we plan our big graduation art.

Content:
First think of what to make. Draw it light with pencil. Use bright colours. Make it beautiful. Show your teacher your plan.

Class activity:
Children draw their graduation art plan on paper. Share with friends.

Evaluation questions:
What are you making for graduation?
What materials do you need?
Show me your drawing.

Summary:
We planned our graduation art today.

topics.title: Class mural design
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify a mural theme
The pupils should be able to draw simple outlines

Introduction:
Last week we made art plans. Today we make a big class art.

Content:
A mural is a big painting on wall. We all help make it. First we vote for a theme. We draw the outline with thick pencil. Everyone adds something.

Class activity:
Children vote for mural theme. Draw outline on big paper.

Evaluation questions:
What is our mural about?
Who drew the outline?
What will you add to the mural?

Summary:
We designed our class mural together.

topics.title: Mural painting
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to paint assigned sections
The pupils should be able to blend colors

Introduction:
We have our mural design. Today we paint it together.

Content:
Painting is fun. Use brush or sponge. Fill your space. Wash brush between colors. Mix colors to make new ones. Work together nicely.

Class activity:
Children paint sections of the mural. Share colors and tools.

Evaluation questions:
What color are you using?
How do you blend colors?
Show me your painted part.

Summary:
We painted our class mural as a team.

topics.title: Card making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a thank you card
The pupils should be able to make a pop-up element

Introduction:
Mummy and daddy love surprises. Today we make cards for them.

Content:
A card shows love. Fold paper in half. Draw a picture inside. Add words like thank you. Make a pop-up surprise by cutting and folding.

Class activity:
Children make thank you cards with pop-up elements.

Evaluation questions:
What will you write in your card?
How do you make a pop-up?
Show me your finished card.

Summary:
We made beautiful cards for our parents.

topics.title: Book mark craft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to design a bookmark
The pupils should be able to decorate it nicely

Introduction:
We use bookmarks in books. Today we make our own special ones.

Content:
A bookmark marks your page. Cut paper rectangle. Decorate with colors, stickers or drawings. Make it strong. Give to a friend as gift.

Class activity:
Children design and decorate bookmarks to give away.

Evaluation questions:
What does a bookmark do?
How will you decorate yours?
Who will you give it to?

Summary:
We made lovely bookmarks for friends.

topics.title: Crown and cap craft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to measure materials for crown
The pupils should be able to decorate their graduation crown

Introduction:\ graduation is coming. We need special crowns to wear.

Content:
A crown shows you are special. Measure paper to fit head. Cut in a circle. Add decorations like gems or colors. Make it fit well.

Class activity:
Children measure, cut and decorate graduation crowns.

Evaluation questions:
What is a crown for?
How do you make it fit your head?
Show me your decorations.

Summary:
We made beautiful graduation crowns.

topics.title: Drum making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to decorate a drum
The pupils should be able to play a simple beat

Introduction:
We love music. Today we make drums and play them.

Content:
A drum makes sound. Use tin can or clay pot. Decorate with colors or patterns. Hit with hands or sticks. Make different sounds.

Class activity:
Children decorate drums and play class beat together.

Evaluation questions:
What can you use to make a drum?
How do you play your drum?
What sound does your drum make?

Summary:
We made drums and played music together.

topics.title: Dance and drama art
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to paint their face for play
The pupils should be able to help make costumes

Introduction:
We will have a play. Today we get ready with face paint and costumes.

Content:
Face paint changes how you look. Use safe paints. Draw patterns on face. Costumes are special clothes for play. Make them colorful.

Class activity:
 Children help paint faces and make simple costumes.

Evaluation questions:
What is face paint for?
How do you help make costumes?
Show me your face paint design.

Summary:
We got ready for our play with face paint and costumes.

topics.title: Photography walk
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to look through a camera
The pupils should be able to frame a picture

Introduction:
We can take pictures of nice things. Today we walk and take photos.

Content:
A camera takes pictures. Look through the lens. Hold it steady. Frame what you want to capture. Take picture of school garden.

Class activity:
Children take turns taking pictures of school garden.

Evaluation questions:
What does a camera do?
How do you hold a camera?
What did you take a picture of?

Summary:
We took pictures of our school garden.

topics.title: Graduation gallery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to display their art works
The pupils should be able to appreciate others' art

Introduction:
We made so much art this term. Today we show everyone.

Content:
A gallery shows art. Display all your work neatly. Put name on each piece. Walk around and see friends' art. Give awards for best work.

Class activity:
Children set up art gallery and give awards.

Evaluation questions:
What is a gallery?
Which art is your favorite?
Who gets an award today?

Summary:
We celebrated our art at graduation gallery.
